doc.title: Jamey Aebersold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 26, 2022

title: J.J. Johnson's note about the Burnin' play-a-long
summary: Aebersold reads a 1994 letter from J.J. Johnson praising the play-a-longs and the fast Volume 61.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: I must say that when you said Charlie Parker and I don’t know what to think about that, if you see over my shoulder you see your “All Bird” book. When I bought that and tried to play along with it, I said, “I don’t know what to think about this except I’m not ready for it.”

Let me show you something. You know musicians, we’ve always aspired to be able to play fast, fast, fast and being able to play what we’re actually thinking at a fast tempo and make it swing, make it cook. Here’s the fall of 1994, J.J. Johnson. I’ll read it to you: I’ll read it to you. He says, “Dear Jamey, Leaving for Japan in a few days. Chops are just awful. Thank God for Aebersold [he means the play-a-longs to warm up with]. Jamey, I really do appreciate you sending me all of the goodies. [that is, whenever a new play-a- long would come out I’d send it to him.] Well my fastest one, which was the emphasis was on playing fast was Volume 61 called Burnin’ B-U-R-N-I-N-apostrophe. He says
Can you read that last part?
Yeah it says “Burnin’ long line well question mark, question mark, J.J.” And I thought that was really cute.
That’s terrific and I’m glad you held on to it too.
Let me ask you, I’m sorry, go ahead.
